New vuln in the Runas ALL keyword specification in sudoers. Patch up quick if you're using it.

Pretty simple vuln. When specifying a certain program to be run as ALL in sudoers (i.e. The user running the program can run it in the context of any user they desire) there is a vulnerability in the function which handles specifying the user to run by userid which allows command execution as root even when execution as root is speficially disabled.

For example if you wanted to specify allowing user voat to run /bin/sh in the context of any user except root you would Edit sudoers as follows

voat = (ALL, !root) /bin/sh

To run the program as a given user you can use the following command

sudo -u otheruser /bin/sh

You can also specify users by userid using #(id) so for example to run in the context of uid 1488

sudo - u#1488 /bin/sh

In the case of user voat he is not allowed to run as root so typing -u#0 would return with an error

However, due to lack of validation this input check only checks if the uid entered is equal to the ones disallowed (0 in this case) or not. Because of this, in the case - 1 or 4294967295 is entered as the uid it gets past the check as they arent equal to 0, but because they are invalid ids they return a 0, allowing execution as root even when specifically denied.

For the case above where voat is allowed to run /bin/sh in the context of any user besides root, the following command would allow root command exec

sudo #u-1 /bin/sh
